page.overview:
Who is El Huracán?

Hurakan, also known as El Huracán, was the Mexican-Lacandon owner and ruler of the secretive criminal colony island of Lagrimas Negras. The character served as a primary antagonist of Charlie Higson's 2007 Young Bond novel, Hurricane Gold.

Born circa 1866 to a runaway slave named Gaspar deep inside the rainforests of southern Mexico, Hurakan was named after the Mayan god of wind and storms. Raised among the Lacandon Indians, the restless boy left home at the age of twelve and worked as a guide for jungle loggers, before becoming a sailor and eventually labouring on a sugar plantation in Cuba. There he fought against the United States during the Spanish–American War of 1898. He subsequently travelled to Mexico and fought in the 1910-1920 revolution, riding with Pancho Villa's elite cavalry, Los Dorados, the Golden Ones. There he acquired a new Spanish name, El Huracán, the Hurricane.

By the time he left Mexico, El Huracán had been married four times (and outlived each of his wives), had been a train robber, an encyclopedia salesman, a banker, a gunrunner, a bootlegger, a farmer, a shopkeeper and a politician. He had drilled for oil and dug for gold; becoming a very wealthy and influential figure. In 1918, at the age of fifty-two, he finally visited the now-abandoned penal colony of Lagrimas Negras to see where his father had come from. Keen to rid themselves of the island, the Americans sold it to El Huracán for $35,000 (equivalent to approximately $657,000 in 2021). With the help of his loyal followers, he turned the dilapidated island into a secretive luxury resort for wanted criminals. Unbeknownst to his desperate guests, El Huracán served as both their permanent host and jailer, and enriched himself at their expense - draining their ill-gotten wealth and eventually enslaving them to labour on the island.

Circa February 1934, criminal and mercenary Theda Glass arrived at Lagrimas Negras; having initially been contracted by the Japanese to obtain stolen US naval documents from her former associate, smuggler Jack Stone. Instead, she sold the documents to El Huracán in exchange for a life of supposed luxury. Shortly afterwards, two teenagers - James Bond and Precious Stone - arrived on the island in pursuit of Glass. Both were detained by El Huracán who forbade them to leave. Over the course of their incarceration he grew fond of Bond and began to groom him as his potential successor. However, the boy and his friend intended to escape and they tricked the initially reluctant El Huracán into allowing them to run his torturous rat run - La Avenida de la Muerte, the Avenue of Death. The teenagers worked their way to freedom, sabotaging the Avenue's final impossible death-trap, and were graciously permitted to leave; taking the stolen naval documents with them. The fate of the island and its de-facto ruler are unknown.
